title: Death of the Young
subtitle: Both life and death are equally insignificant.

items.text: Death of the Young

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Heh. Don't worry so much, Paul! We'll find glory on the battlefield! No man can stop us as long as we stick together!

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text:
Come on, let's join the war and prove ourselves to Mr. Mühlenberge. Think how proud your parents will be—their son, 
a war hero!

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: Eberhard!

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Goddamn! Where's Dieterich?

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: He and Baethke are dead! Grab that gun. We need to go! Move!

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Do you think we'll win, Paul?

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: I don't know, my friend. I think I just want to go home.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Dieterich, Baethke, and Elvin ... What did they die for if we just give up?

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Hang in there, Paul! The only way to make their sacrifice count is to win!

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: We promised we'd go home together! Paul ... Paul!
Major, the past is in the past. You can't change anything by letting yourself be overcome by sorrow.
Don't forget that victory is the only thing that matters, and we can give it to you.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Give it to me? How?
I'll make you a true hero, one without fear or hesitation.
Smoke and blood fade into the distance.
Eberhard lies on a wooden board dragged by some unseen force.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: *cough*
He swallows air like a drowning man, and immediately the foul stench of decay fills his lungs.
The dragging stops.

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: You're awake.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Paul?
But the man behind the mask says nothing. He only offers a hand.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Ah. My head ... It hurts.
Eberhard struggles to adjust to his surroundings, taking a long time to find focus.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Where are you taking me?

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: Montpaix. The Foundation may have some cure for the spell you have fallen under.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: No ... No ...
Still dazed after the ordeal, he can only mutter in denial.
He looks around, searching for something to brace against, eventually finding the ground. He takes off his hat and scratches at his straw-like golden hair.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: I ... Good heavens. What did I do?
He still can't find his breath, each gasp of air only making the choking sensation worse.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: That deserter ... I ordered Rudolph to pull the trigger. But I was the one who killed him.

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: The other lives. Erich saw to that.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: He wasn't the only one. So many have died, and I was the one that sent them to their deaths.
Eberhard lowers his head, holding his gaze at a small patch of soil beneath him.
Charon watches him, adjusting his dark cloak.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Do you remember, Paul? There was a poem by Goethe, no, Schiller maybe? Ah, those days at school feel like a fairy tale now.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Mr. Mühlenberge asked you and Dieterich to write it out on the blackboard. You two didn't even know where to start. I remember I thought he was going to snap you both in two.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Just a few months later, we were here. Dieterich died that very first day.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Do you remember how we cried that night? We thought it would be the saddest day of our lives.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: We ran out of tears before anything else.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: I'm cold, Paul.

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: A fear long absent is growing inside you again. Hold on to it. You'll warm up.
Eberhard clenches his teeth and braces himself.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: This is the place you found, isn't it? Where Franz was buried.

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: He lies below us.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: There are so many graves, but I'm still alive. Why, Paul, why am I not lying among them?

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: The living speak of luck. The rest are silent.
The answer doesn't satisfy, but the lone survivor cannot find a new question. After a long silence, he speaks again.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: I wish I could forget it all now. If I didn't know what happened, I wouldn't—No, no, it's, it's not right for me to ask that ...

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: But I am still alive. Is there anything I can do for them?

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: That isn't a question for the dead. I can't tell you what to do, Eberhard.
Eberhard reaches into his coat pocket but finds it empty. He stifles a helpless grunt.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: You mentioned Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: You remember.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: What about the Foundation? You talked to them too, right? Do you really think they can stop this war?

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: They pursue peace, but it cannot be found by their efforts alone.
He turns from the hill to the woods. Through the thicket and further lies the town of Montpaix.
Eberhard closes his eyes and waits for his thoughts to settle.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Come on. Let's go see Montpaix again.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: I was about to pay a visit to Mr. Mühlenberge when someone from Army Command said the colonel wanted to see me.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: I was taken to a meeting room with many other officers. I recognized them. I knew many had just been promoted like me.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Colonel Hirschfelder showed up to give us a speech—yes, yes, the same colonel who was assassinated after the parley.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: "The time has come when our nation calls for heroes," he said, "with our foremost goal to create a prosperous new world for our children."

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: "We have fought valiantly, and now the war turns in our favor. We stand but one step away from total victory, yet it is at this very moment that our soldiers have lost their courage."

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: "They waste their time looting every barn, cellar, and shed in search of treasure and drink to numb their fears, delaying our operations."

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: "Their greed and cowardice have spread through our army like a malignant tumor. Fortunately, we have found a cure."

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: "An organization that believes in the promise of our victory has provided us with an extraordinary development ..."

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: That's all I remember. I don't have a mind for technology, but it just washed the fear off me.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Thinking about it now, we must have been like lab rats to them. As soon as they finished their ritual, we became so sure of our victory that we began yelling and singing as one. We were just fresh-faced boys again, thirsty for a war we'd forgotten.
The hiss of static echoes through the spacious room, then fades.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: I think that's enough for now. That was a recording from a German major we encountered in Montpaix.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: I intend to submit a report with full details, including his entire statement and an explanation for our inquiries.
The head of the frontline investigation quiets, awaiting further instructions from the decision makers at the rear.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Manus Vindictae is moving quicker than any of us could've imagined.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: But none of these makes sense.
Pedra has returned from the front, still shaken from the assassination attempt.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: If they came to this era at the same time as we did, how could they have already infiltrated the military higher-ups in such a short time?

items.speaker: Z
items.text: We've already theorized that Arcana may now possess the power to rewrite history.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Which means going forward. Any records from history as we once knew it will be unreliable for estimating their strength.
Pedra falls into heavy silence.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Pedra, what were the other representatives' opinions concerning Manus Vindictae?

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: They all denied its existence.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: I see. It seems as though we're left with no other option but to change policies.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: No. We can't resort to such radical measures.
The Doves' representative states his position in advance.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: The Foundation risks alienating any potential allies if we act too aggressively now. This war will not be the end of our fight. We will need to rely on their cooperation in the future.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: And that requires trust and a sense of security.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: On the subject of governments, I have some news to report.
Creius's voice resurfaces in the conference hall.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: A man of the Inter-Factional Committee paid a secret visit to Montpaix, hoping to obtain intel about the Manus.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: A secret visit?
As a fellow politician, Pedra immediately grasps the true intent behind their visit.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: What did they say? Do they intend to use our intel against the heads of their Army Command?

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: You've guessed it. If their government manages to rein in the army, it'll be much easier to reach a ceasefire.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: But if anyone were to find out, we might be accused of interfering in their internal affairs. Have you considered that, Creius?

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Officially, the Foundation never made any contact with their government. All I did was have a candid conversation with a man about my concerns for his people.
He stresses one key detail.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: At any rate, they haven't any reason to expose their cooperation with us.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: There are simply too many uncertainties to consider.
The politician, accustomed to checks and balances, catches the implication of a factional dispute.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: History will only be restored to its rightful track if the peaceful factions on each side can rise to power and stop this war. This has been our goal from the beginning.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: It doesn't matter which era we end up in. We always benefit from a political climate that is friendly to the Foundation. That's undeniable.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: What do you think, Pedra?
He removes his glasses and rubs his eyes.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: I might be able to persuade some of the other Committee members to support this proposal. If we're certain of this course of action, then we'll have to provide intel to those seeking peace in all governments involved.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Good. No faction should put their own goals above those of the Foundation's.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: We'll need more to verify that major's statement. Send investigators to search other regions and report everything they see. Creius, continue your investigation. Follow every possible lead.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Understood. We'll dig up whatever they have buried.
